summary: Enga Teramoto worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professeur at Otani University from 1915 and as a lecturer at Kyoto University in 1920.
Enichi Ocho was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo around 1926 to 1929. He later served at Otani University as professor emeritus from around 1949 to 1976.

Enryo Inoue worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at Niigata Prefectural Nagaoka High School, Higashi Hongan-ji Temple, and the University of Tokyo, he founded Toyo University, serving there from circa 1887 to 1906, and held a post at Keihoku Gakuen Hakusan High School.

Ensho Kanakura worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo and under Yukio Sakamoto. His career included posts at Tohoku University (1923–1960), Rissho University, Miyagi University of Education (1966–1969), and the Japan Academy (1952–1987).
Ensho Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University. His studies were supervised by Eshō Mikogami, with Ryoji Oka and Hiromi Yoshimura serving as committee members.

Enshu Kurumiya specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a Ph.D. at the Australian National University around 1970–1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University.

Erberto Lo Bue specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London around 1975–1981 and held posts at the University of Bologna and the University of Milan.

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University around 1997–2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton. He also studied under Chongren He, Xiaoxun He, Zhiben He, Xi Aniu, and He Xuewen.

Eric Huntington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago around 2006–2013 under Gary A. Tubb, with Christian K. Wedemeyer and Rob Linrothe on his committee.

Eric J. Sharpe was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Manchester from circa 1955 to 1958. He held posts at the University of Manchester, Lancaster University, and the University of Sydney.

Eric M. Greene is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley around 2005–2012 under Robert H. Sharf. Around 2017, he was appointed assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University.
Eric Reinders is a scholar in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned MA degrees from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erich Frauwallner was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Vienna from 1918 to 1921. He held an editorial post at the University of Vienna and founded the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens.

Erich Haenisch was a scholar of sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, Leipzig University, the University of Göttingen, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, and founded the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a scholar of philosophy who held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg around 1912–1913 and the University of Marburg around 1913–1940.
Erik Braun works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University from around 2001 to 2008, where Janet Gyatso served as his doctoral supervisor.

Erik Haarh was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who earned a doctor's degree from the University of Copenhagen around 1948–1969. He held a post at the Royal Danish Library from circa 1953 to 1975.

Erik J. Hammerstrom works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at Indiana University around 2004–2010 and became an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University around 2010.
Erik Mueggler is a scholar of sinology who studied at Deep Springs College, Cornell University, and Johns Hopkins University. He held a post at the University of Michigan in 2019.
